full_judgment: 5. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaintiffs contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, and since the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit property as such their suit for partition on payment of fixed court fees is not maintainable. The schedule land was auction purchased by Shaham Ali in revenue sale and his grandfather took over lease of 2 kani, 7 ganda, 1 kara and 1 kranti land by registered patta. Defendant No. 4 son of defendant No. 1 purchased 1 kani land from the gradual heirs of C.S. tenant Latu and he is in possession. Defendant No. 1 purchased 14 ganda land from Karam Ali who got the same as heirs of Abdul Ali and Bacha Miah. He also purchased 3 ganda land from Asma Khatun who got the land from her husband Ahmed Ali. Thus the defendant No. 1 got 4 kani, 4 panda, 1 kara and 3 kranti land in schedule-1 properties. The documents submitted by the plaintiffs are all forged and fraudulent in respect of schedule-1 suit properties. The schedule-2 suit property was purchased by Mosharaf Ali in rent execution case who sold the same to the defendant No. 1 by registered kabala. The land in schedule 3 belonged to Abdur Rahman who sold 5 ganda land to defendant No. 1 in the benami of his sister's husband Faizur Rahman. Thereafter the said Abdur Rahman died leaving his son Kabir Ahmed who inherited the remaining 5 ganda land in schedule-3 and the defendant No. 1 also purchased the said 5 ganda land from Kabir in the benami of his cousin Sultan.
